pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If a's six-part Sufficient(K,O,I) definition was derived independently from a different literature source (e.g. directly from database-theory 'sufficient statistic' concepts, as seen elsewhere in this batch's RP0358) without textual awareness of b's Astrom extraction, the match would be convergent reuse of a common information-theoretic idea rather than a extending b.

rationale_evidence.anchor: if an operation legality decision is L(o,K), then there must exist no required information X such that L(o,K,X) cannot be reduced to L(o,K) unless X is explicitly defined as an external dependency.
rationale_evidence.statement: Proposes an information-theoretic reducibility test distinguishing state from external context: a legality decision that silently depends on information beyond K is either evidence that K is incomplete, or that the extra information X must be explicitly declared an external dependency rather than folded into K — a discipline against 'arbitrarily putting every useful object inside K'.
